seats: a secular academic scholar of the Bible

fixes.row: “Heaven” standing alone: “against heaven”, “from heaven or from men”, “Heaven rules”
fixes.why: Berean prints 'against heaven' but the Hebrew under it (Ps 75:6 in the Hebrew numbering) is הַמָּרוֹם 'the high', not שָׁמַיִם. The hub lists it as a heaven-word verse and under a note about a standing-alone 'heaven'. The verse is in the hand pick list, not found by rule.
fixes.fix: Remove Ps 75:5 from the heaven rows (or place it under others with a note: 'the Berean prints heaven for the Hebrew for the high').

fixes.row: In heaven and on earth: above and below, between heaven and earth
fixes.why: Phil 2:10 has ἐπουρανίων (adjective, 'of the heavens'), not οὐρανός. It sits in this noun row and also in the adjective row 'Heavenly realms...'. One word is counted under two forms and the noun row displays it as the noun's use.
fixes.fix: Drop Phil 2:10 from the noun row; keep it in the adjective row. Same check for any other noun-row verse whose only heaven word is ἐπουράνιος.

fixes.row: Heaven and earth pass away; the heavens shaken, darkened, rolled up; signs in heaven
fixes.why: The label and note frame the row as the end of the present heaven and earth (the note speaks of 'renewed or replaced'). Most of its Old Testament verses are prophetic or poetic imagery inside oracles against Babylon, Edom and Egypt, the day of the LORD, or Job and a psalm. Filed under the heading 'Heaven and earth pass away' next to Matt 24:35 and 2 Pet 3:10 they read as one doctrine of cosmic end, which later readers drew but the verses do not state. Also 'signs' are three different things (Pharisees demanding a sign, Joel's wonders, Rev's signs).
fixes.fix: Relabel: 'The heavens shaken, darkened, rolled up, or passing away'. Add to the note that the Old Testament verses stand in oracles against named nations or the day of the LORD (Isa 13 Babylon, Isa 34 Edom, Ezek 32 Pharaoh) and that the page does not say they speak of the end of the world. Lead the examples with Isa 34:4 or Isa 13:10, not Matt 5:18.

fixes.row: Heaven and earth pass away; the heavens shaken, darkened, rolled up; signs in heaven
fixes.why: 'A sign from heaven' demanded of Jesus, Ahaz asked to ask a sign 'from the heights of heaven', and God's signs and wonders in Dan 6:27 are not the heavens being shaken. They belong with 'a voice, a sound or a light from heaven' (what comes from heaven) or stand in their own row. Putting them under 'pass away' cuts the story-line of 'from heaven' apart from itself.
fixes.fix: Move Matt 16:1, Mark 8:11, Luke 11:16 to the row 'The heavens opened...a voice, a sound or a light from heaven' (relabel 'a voice, a light, a sign from heaven'); leave Isa 7:11 and Dan 6:27 with it as well, or drop 'signs in heaven' from the label.

fixes.row: Taken up into heaven (Elijah; Jesus, at the right hand of God); the Son of Man, the Lord Jesus, coming with the clouds of heaven or from heaven
fixes.why: Two different claims share a label (going up; coming back) and the second half of the label names 'the Son of Man, the Lord Jesus' as the one coming. Dan 7:13 ('one like a son of man') is filed under a heading that already identifies him as Jesus, so the Old Testament verse is heard under a New Testament name. The note says the page does not say how they relate, yet the label says it.
fixes.fix: Split into two rows: (a) 'Taken up into heaven: Elijah; Jesus' (2 Kgs 2:1, 2:11 first; Mark 16:19, Acts 1:11, Acts 7:55-56, Heb 4:14, 9:24, John 3:13); (b) 'Coming with the clouds of heaven or from heaven' with Dan 7:13 first, labelled 'one like a son of man', then Matt 24:30, 26:64, Mark 14:62, 1 Thess 1:10, 2 Thess 1:7, Phil 3:20. Keep the existing note on (b). This also brings the count to 27 rows, so see the merge below.

fixes.row: Not named in the verse: “He”, “Him”, “the One”, “the second man”, “the Lord”, “a Master”
fixes.why: This row is sorted by grammar (no name in the verse), which cuts apart what the story keeps together: the ascension (Luke 24:51, Acts 1:2, 1:10) from Acts 1:11 and Luke's other ascent verses; John 6:33, 6:50 from the bread-from-heaven verses in 'Jesus: came down from heaven' (John 6:32-58). Eph 6:9 and Col 4:1 ('a Master in heaven') have nothing to do with descending or ascending and sit oddly here. Rev 19:11 'Faithful and True' is a title, not 'no name'.
fixes.fix: Keep the row (it is the honest way to avoid naming), but (1) move Eph 6:9 and Col 4:1 out to the row 'The LORD, God, in heaven' only if the page is willing to say 'Master' is God, otherwise own small group or the Every other use row; (2) add to the note a pointer: 'John 6:33, 6:50 belong with the bread from heaven (row 16); Luke 24:51, Acts 1:2, 1:10 with Acts 1:11 (row 17)'; (3) change the label to 'Not named in the verse: “He”, “the One”, “the second man”, “the Lord”, “a Master”, “Faithful and True”'.

fixes.row: Fallen or cast down from heaven; war in heaven
fixes.why: A single row for Isa 14:12, Luke 10:18 and Rev 12 presents a fall of Satan as one thread by position alone. The row also carries stars falling (Rev 8:10, 9:1, Dan 8:10), Lam 2:1 (Zion cast down from heaven to earth) which are not about a fallen being. The note says readers part, but the lead examples (Isa 14:12, Luke 10:18, Rev 12:7-8) are exactly the chain of the traditional reading.
fixes.fix: Lead with Lam 2:1 and Dan 8:10, then Isa 14:12, then Luke 10:18, then Rev 12; or relabel 'Cast down from heaven to earth: a king, a star, a city, Satan, the dragon and his angels' so the row names what each verse says. Move Rev 12:7-8 to the angels row only (it is already there) or mark it as in both.

fixes.row: Your heavenly Father; My heavenly Father
fixes.why: Matt 23:9 ('one Father, who is in heaven') uses the adjective yet sits in 'Heavenly realms, things, bodies...' while 'Your heavenly Father' is its own row. Rows 'Your Father in heaven' (16 verses, οὐρανός) and 'Your heavenly Father' (6, οὐράνιος) say the same thing in Matthew; apart is right for different words, but the 26 rows are over the 25 budget.
fixes.fix: Move Matt 23:9 to 'Your heavenly Father'. Keep it a separate row from 'Your Father in heaven' (different words) but add a cross-pointer in each note, or fold it as a second line inside a combined row whose label names both phrases separately, if a row has to go.

fixes.row: Under all heaven; the ends and four winds of heaven; reaching to heaven, higher than the heavens, ascending to heaven
fixes.why: 77 verses under a four-clause label is the hub's largest and loosest row: where something is (under heaven), its extent (ends of heaven, four winds), and going up (ascending). The ascents (Gen 28:12, Gen 11:4, Isa 14:13, Prov 30:4, Rom 10:6, 2 Cor 12:2) are one story line of reaching for heaven that is cut off from 'Taken up into heaven' and the Isa 14 / Gen 11 'ascend' pairing.
fixes.fix: Split 'ascending to heaven, reaching to heaven' (Gen 11:4, 28:12, Deut 30:12, Ps 139:8, Prov 30:4, Isa 14:13, Amos 9:2, Rom 10:6, 2 Cor 12:2) from 'under all heaven / ends of heaven / four winds'. Add a note that 2 Cor 12:2 is Paul's own account of being caught up.

worker_points.point: 1. Rows 21, 22, 26: heaven at death or new heaven and earth
worker_points.why: Each carries a no-side note and the label says only what the verses say (kept in heaven, a new heaven coming). No row asserts the intermediate state. A door to Luke 23:43, Phil 1:23, 2 Cor 5:8 would help but is not a text fault.

worker_points.point: 2. Row 4: pass away and signs in one row
worker_points.why: They should not read as one claim, and the Old Testament oracle imagery sits under an end-of-world heading. See the two row-4 fixes.

worker_points.point: 3. Row 18: is the 'readers take them of Jesus' sentence a lean?
worker_points.why: It states only what readers do and names examples, which is acceptable, but a sentence that narrows 'the Lord' to the Father or Christ leaves out other readers (an angel, the LORD of the Old Testament in Heb 1). Soften to 'readers take them differently; the page does not choose' and point to the neighbouring rows. Eph 6:9 and Col 4:1 are misplaced.

worker_points.point: 4. Rows 16, 17, 19: the persons by hand; Dan 7:13 placement
worker_points.why: Persons are named by hand in the verse text, so rows 16 and 19 are fine. Row 17 fails: Dan 7:13 sits under a heading that names Jesus, and 'taken up' and 'coming' are different claims. See the split.
Lead examples are the traditional chain. Reorder and relabel so each verse is named for what it says (a king, a star, a city, Satan).
Matthew's phrase as written, the parallels named, no claim that they are one. Fair to a scholar.

worker_points.point: 7. Row 1: host of heaven in one row
worker_points.why: The note sorts idolatry, the host beside the LORD's throne and the Queen of Heaven. One row does not claim one host. Acceptable; Jer 7:18 and 44:17-25 'Queen of Heaven' could be called a different figure, which the note already does.

The note is fair, but Ps 75:5 does not contain the heaven word (marom, 'the high'), and Ps 73:9 is plainly a parallel with earth, not a standing-alone use. Remove Ps 75:5 and consider moving Ps 73:9 to 'The heavens declare, praise... / Every other use'.

worker_points.point: 9. Row 5: Acts 4:12 and a door to salvation
worker_points.why: Leaving Acts 4:12 in the row as written and not leading with it is right. A door to the salvation card is the owner's choice.
No equation of persons; Jesus' 'Father, Lord of heaven and earth' is under the one he addresses, as written.
The note says plainly that the Berean prints 'midair' and 'overhead' for μεσουράνημα and does not call the sky heaven.

missing.what: A reader-visible statement at the top of the hub that the Hebrew שָׁמַיִם and Greek οὐρανός are one word for sky and for God's dwelling, so a reader does not take 'heaven' in Gen 1 as the place of Matt 6:9. It is only in row 1's note, where a reader of the later rows may never see it.

Genesis 1:8 'God called the expanse sky' and Ps 148:4 'highest heavens' / 'waters above the heavens' (the heavens as a structure with waters above) are not distinguished from the 'God made the heavens' row; a reader of the original sees a layered cosmos that the English hides.

Heaven as a sphere in the Hebrew Scriptures' own terms ('heaven of heavens', Deut 10:14, 1 Kgs 8:27) is mixed into the throne and dwelling row with Rev 4:2 and Heb 9:24; the Hebrew Scriptures' own picture could lead.

examples_checked: 26 of 26 rows' examples show their label (weakest: Hebrews 4:14 under 'Taken up into heaven' says passed through the heavens; Ps 73:9 under 'Heaven standing alone' is a plain parallel with earth)
summary: The hub keeps to the text and its no-side notes are sound, but two verses sit under heaven words they do not contain (Ps 75:5 marom, Phil 2:10 ἐπουράνιος), and the Old Testament oracle imagery under 'pass away', Dan 7:13 under a Jesus label, and the fall-from-heaven lead examples read a later doctrine back. Rows that cut a story apart (the ascent and descent verses split across 'taken up', 'not named' and 'ascending', and 'signs from heaven' filed under 'pass away') should be regrouped before showing.
